I have farmed this land for 50 years, so I know what works here in Quzhou. My soil is a bit alkaline loam, decent organic matter after years of returning maize straw. With only 6 mu and two mouths, I cannot afford a bad harvest, but I also learned from the county technicians and the Science Backyard students that we old farmers used to over-fertilize — I have cut back some compared to 20 years ago, but not too much. Rather waste 20 yuan of urea than lose 500 yuan of cabbage.

For **spring cabbage** (planted March, harvested late May): cabbage is a heavy feeder and the money crop. I will use hybrid seed — the local seed dealer sells "Zhonggan 21" which my neighbors had good heads with. Base fertilizer: about 3 bags of compound (15-15-15) per mu plus 2 carts of chicken manure I got cheap from the layer farm. Topdress urea twice. Total around 22 kg N, 10 kg P, 15 kg K per mu. Irrigate 5 times from well — cabbage needs steady water or the heads split. Spray maybe 4 times for diamondback moth and aphids, they are bad here.

For **summer maize** (planted June after cabbage, harvested late September): Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335 hybrid, same as everyone in the village. I rotary-till the residue in. Maize after cabbage — the soil still has leftover fertilizer from cabbage, so I reduce N a bit. About 16 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K per mu. One base application, one topdress at big trumpet stage. Irrigate 3 times — jointing, tasseling, grain fill. Spray once or twice for corn borer. Expect around 600 kg.

For **winter spinach** (sown October, harvested through winter): I grow improved overwintering variety. Spinach is short season, doesn't need much. 8 kg N, 4 kg P, 5 kg K per mu. Irrigate twice before frost, once after green-up. Usually no spray needed in cold weather. Around 2500 kg/mu if winter is mild.

I plough once a year before cabbage, rotary-till between the other crops — saves diesel money.

decision.reasoning_summary: With 6 mu and 50 years of experience, I keep my cabbage-maize-spinach rotation because it uses the land all year and cabbage pays my biggest bills. I have cut fertilizer somewhat from my younger days after the county technicians showed us we were overusing, but I still lean a bit high on cabbage since a lost head of cabbage costs far more than an extra bag of urea. I use hybrid seed for cabbage and maize like all my neighbors, plough once before cabbage and rotary-till between crops to save fuel, and irrigate from my well according to each crop's critical stages.
